data.narrative:
Augury, founded by Gal Shaul and Saar Yoskovitz, is a Series F-stage robotics and manufacturing software company that has raised $369M to date. The broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector contains nine peer companies—one public (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Locus Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics—though comparable transaction data remains sparse at Augury's scale and stage.

Given data constraints, valuation relies primarily on stage-progression analysis. Using Augury's $369M total raised as a baseline and applying a 1.3x step-up multiplier typical of Series F advancement, this method implies a valuation of $480M. The peer-median approach could not be applied; insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables (fewer than three datapoints meeting narrow filters) preclude reliable benchmarking, and a broad sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The triangulated range is $408M (low) to $552M (median-anchored), centered at $480M. Key uncertainties include the absence of recent comparable Series F+ transactions in frontier robotics, variation in revenue multiples and burn profiles across the peer set, and limited public market data. The valuation should be stress-tested against management guidance on path to profitability and customer concentration risk.
